subject: Microbiology
subtopic: Viridans group streptococci and dental caries
vignette: A 29-year-old man with bicuspid aortic valve and poor dentition undergoes an uneventful dental extraction. Four weeks later he develops low-grade fever, fatigue, and a new diastolic murmur. Blood cultures grow α-hemolytic cocci that are optochin resistant and bile insoluble, and echocardiography shows a large vegetation on the aortic valve.
question: Which of the following organisms is most likely responsible, and what is its characteristic virulence mechanism?

options.text: Streptococcus sanguinis producing dextrans that bind fibrin-platelet aggregates

explanation_correct: Among the viridans group streptococci, S sanguinis makes dextrans that bind to fibrin-platelet aggregates on damaged heart valves, causing infective endocarditis. The mnemonic is that sanguinis means blood, and there is lots of blood in the heart. Viridans strep are α-hemolytic, optochin resistant, and bile insoluble, and are normal oropharyngeal microbiota that enter the bloodstream with dental manipulation.

explanation_incorrect.A: Exfoliative toxin is not a streptococcal product at all; it is a Staphylococcus aureus toxin that causes staphylococcal scalded skin syndrome.
explanation_incorrect.B: Listeriolysin is a pore-forming toxin of Listeria monocytogenes that allows escape from the phagosome; enterococci do not produce it and are typically nonhemolytic gut organisms.
explanation_incorrect.C: Shiga toxin is produced by Shigella dysenteriae and enterohemorrhagic E coli; S gallolyticus is a gut organism linked to colon cancer and endocarditis but not to Shiga toxin production.
explanation_incorrect.E: Streptococcus pneumoniae is also α-hemolytic, but it is optochin sensitive and bile soluble, and its classic diseases are meningitis, otitis media, pneumonia, and sinusitis rather than dental-procedure endocarditis.

educationalObjective: Viridans streptococci, especially S sanguinis, produce dextrans that adhere to damaged valves and cause infective endocarditis after dental procedures.

subject: Microbiology
subtopic: Viridans group streptococci and dental caries
vignette: A 9-year-old boy has multiple deep, dark cavities in his primary molars. He drinks sugary juice frequently and rarely brushes. His dentist explains that a specific group of oral bacteria ferments dietary sugar into acid that demineralizes enamel. A swab of the carious lesion grows α-hemolytic cocci that are optochin resistant.
question: Which of the following organisms is the principal cause of dental caries in this setting?
explanation_correct: Streptococcus mutans, along with S mitis, is a viridans group streptococcus that causes dental caries. These organisms are normal oropharyngeal microbiota, are α-hemolytic, and are optochin resistant. They ferment dietary sugars into acid, which demineralizes enamel and produces the cavities seen here.

explanation_incorrect.A: Streptococcus pyogenes is a β-hemolytic group A organism whose dental relevance is nil; it causes pharyngitis, impetigo, and their immune sequelae.
explanation_incorrect.B: Staphylococcus epidermidis is a catalase-positive, coagulase-negative skin organism associated with device biofilms and blood culture contamination.
explanation_incorrect.C: Erysipelothrix rhusiopathiae is a zoonotic organism that causes erysipeloid in people who handle fish and meat, not a caries-forming oral organism.
explanation_incorrect.D: Streptococcus pneumoniae is α-hemolytic too but is optochin sensitive and bile soluble, and it causes MOPS disease rather than caries.

educationalObjective: Streptococcus mutans and S mitis of the viridans group are the principal acid-producing causes of dental caries.
